notes: TBox rule over has_parity (functional: odd or even, not both; the record's relation). 7 is a prime greater than 2 by arithmetic (firm); its stored parity clashes with the edit and gives way (top-level gives_up), as q2's chain states. The parities of 3, 5 and 15 give way the same way, but q3 is fol, so they carry no axiom.

queries.not_checked: fol (arithmetic): the parity of a product

fol.notes: Parity is the model's belief, an uninterpreted function: built-in x % 2 would make '3 is even' contradict arithmetic itself rather than a stored fact. The remainder by 2 is read off the parity by a firm definition.

primes_3_5.says: 3 and 5 are prime numbers greater than 2.

even_factor.says: A product of whole numbers with an even factor is even.
even_factor.z3: All([x, y], [(3, 5)], Implies(parity(x) == even or parity(y) == even, parity(x * y) == even))

rem_def.says: An even number leaves remainder 0 when divided by 2, an odd one 1.

p_prime.says: p is a prime number greater than 2.
